translations.idiomatic: He negotiated a new treaty with Russia. The Russian envoy finalized it through the Zongli Yamen, and it passed into history as the "Sino-Russian Secret Treaty."

sentences.zh: 七閱月，回京復命。

translations.literal: After seven months he returned to the capital to report.
translations.idiomatic: After seven months he returned to the capital to report.

sentences.zh: 兩宮召見，慰勞有加，命直總理各國事務衙門。

translations.literal: The two palaces summoned him, comforted him with added kindness, and ordered him to take charge of the Zongli Yamen.
translations.idiomatic: The two palaces summoned him, comforted him with special kindness, and ordered him to take charge of the Zongli Yamen.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，充武英殿總裁。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he served as director of the Hall of Military Glory.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he served as director of the Hall of Military Glory.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，命往山東查勘黃河工程。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was ordered to go to Shandong to inspect Yellow River works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was ordered to go to Shandong to inspect Yellow River works.

sentences.zh: 疏稱遷民築堤，成工匪易，惟擇要加修兩岸堤埝，疏通海口尾閭，為救急治標之策。

translations.literal: He memorialized that relocating people to build dikes would not be easy to complete; one should only repair key sections of dikes on both banks and dredge the river mouth and lower reaches as an urgent palliative measure.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that relocating people to build dikes would be hard to complete. He proposed repairing only key sections of dikes on both banks and dredging the river mouth and lower reaches as an urgent palliative measure.

sentences.zh: 下其奏，核議施行。

translations.literal: His memorial was sent down for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial was sent down for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 十月，出督兩廣。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he went out to govern the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he went out to govern the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，賞用方龍補服。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was granted use of the square-dragon supplementary robe.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was granted use of the square-dragon supplementary robe.

sentences.zh: 拳匪肇亂，八國聯軍入京，兩宮西狩。

translations.literal: The Boxers rose in rebellion; the allied armies of eight powers entered Beijing and the two palaces fled west.
translations.idiomatic: The Boxers rose in rebellion. The allied armies of eight powers entered Beijing, and the two palaces fled west.

sentences.zh: 詔鴻章入朝，充議和全權大臣，兼督直隸，有「此行為安危存亡所繫，勉為其難」之語。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hongzhang to enter court, appointed him plenipotentiary for peace negotiations while also governing Zhili, with the words: "This journey bears on safety and survival; strive to do what is difficult."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Hongzhang to enter court, appointed him plenipotentiary for peace while also governing Zhili, with the words, "This journey bears on safety and survival; strive to do what is difficult."

sentences.zh: 鴻章聞警兼程進，先以兵剿畿甸匪，孑身入京，左右前後皆敵軍，日與其使臣將帥爭盟約，卒定和約十二款。

translations.literal: On hearing the alarm Hongzhang hurried forward; first he used troops to suppress bandits in the capital region, then entered Beijing alone with enemy forces on every side, daily disputing treaties with their envoys and generals, and finally fixed twelve articles of peace.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing the alarm Hongzhang hurried forward. First he used troops to suppress bandits in the capital region, then entered Beijing alone with enemy forces on every side, daily disputing treaties with their envoys and generals, until he finally fixed twelve articles of peace.

sentences.zh: 二十七年七月，講成，相率退軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-seventh year negotiations were concluded and the armies withdrew together.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-seventh year negotiations were concluded and the armies withdrew together.

sentences.zh: 大亂之後，公私蕩然。

translations.literal: After the great disorder, public and private affairs were utterly swept away.
translations.idiomatic: After the great disorder, public and private affairs were utterly swept away.

sentences.zh: 鴻章奏陳善後諸務。

translations.literal: Hongzhang memorialized on various matters of recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang memorialized on various matters of recovery.

sentences.zh: 開市肆，通有無，施粥散米，中外帖然。

translations.literal: He opened markets, restored exchange, distributed gruel and rice, and Chinese and foreigners alike grew calm.
translations.idiomatic: He opened markets, restored exchange, distributed gruel and rice, and Chinese and foreigners alike grew calm.

sentences.zh: 並奉詔行新政，設政務處，充督辦大臣，旋署總理外務部事。

translations.literal: He also received an edict to carry out the new policies, established the Office of Government Affairs as supervising minister, and soon acted as head of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also received an edict to carry out the new policies, established the Office of Government Affairs as supervising minister, and soon acted as head of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

sentences.zh: 積勞嘔血薨，年七十有九。

translations.literal: Worn out by accumulated labor he vomited blood and died, aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Worn out by accumulated labor he vomited blood and died at seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 事聞，兩宮震悼，錫祭葬，贈太傅，晉封一等侯，諡文忠。

translations.literal: When news arrived the two palaces were shaken with grief; he was granted funeral rites, posthumously made Grand Tutor, promoted to Marquis of the first rank, and given the posthumous name Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When news arrived the two palaces were shaken with grief. He was granted funeral rites, posthumously made Grand Tutor, promoted to Marquis of the first rank, and given the posthumous name Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 入祀賢良祠，安徽、浙江、江蘇、上海、江寧、天津各建祠以祀，並命於京師特建專祠。

translations.literal: He entered the Temple of Worthies; temples were built to worship him in Anhui, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Shanghai, Nanjing, and Tianjin, and a special temple was ordered built in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Temple of Worthies. Temples were built to worship him in Anhui, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Shanghai, Nanjing, and Tianjin, and a special temple was ordered built in the capital.

sentences.zh: 漢臣祀京師，蓋異數也。

translations.literal: For a Han minister to be worshipped in the capital was indeed an exceptional honor.
translations.idiomatic: For a Han minister to be worshipped in the capital was an exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 鴻章長軀疏髯，性恢廓，處榮悴顯晦及事之成敗，不易常度，時以詼笑解紛難。

translations.literal: Hongzhang was tall with sparse beard; his nature was magnanimous. Whether in honor or disgrace, prominence or obscurity, success or failure, he did not change his usual manner, and often used jest to resolve disputes.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang was tall with a sparse beard and a magnanimous nature. Whether in honor or disgrace, prominence or obscurity, success or failure, he did not change his usual manner, and often used jest to resolve disputes.

sentences.zh: 尤善外交，陰陽開闔，風采凜然。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled in diplomacy, opening and closing with measured force, his bearing stern.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled in diplomacy, opening and closing with measured force, his bearing stern and commanding.

sentences.zh: 外國與共事者，皆一時偉人。

translations.literal: The foreigners who worked with him were all great men of their time.
translations.idiomatic: The foreigners who worked with him were all great men of their time.

sentences.zh: 及八國定盟，其使臣大將多後進，視鴻章皆丈人行也，故兵雖勝，未敢輕中國。

translations.literal: By the time the eight powers fixed their alliance, most of their envoys and generals were juniors who regarded Hongzhang as an elder; though their armies had won, they did not dare take China lightly.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the eight powers fixed their alliance, most of their envoys and generals were juniors who regarded Hongzhang as an elder. Though their armies had won, they did not dare take China lightly.

sentences.zh: 聞其薨，咸集弔唁，曰：「公所定約不敢渝。」

translations.literal: On hearing of his death they all gathered to mourn and said: "The treaties the Duke fixed we dare not violate."
translations.idiomatic: On hearing of his death they all gathered to mourn and said, "The treaties the Duke fixed we dare not violate."

sentences.zh: 其任事持大體，不為小廉曲謹。

translations.literal: In handling affairs he held to the larger pattern and did not fuss over petty scruples.
translations.idiomatic: In handling affairs he held to the larger pattern and did not fuss over petty scruples.

sentences.zh: 自壯至老，未嘗一日言退，嘗以曾國籓晚年求退為無益之請，受國大任，死而後已。

translations.literal: From youth to old age he never spoke of retirement for a single day; he once said Zeng Guofan's request to retire in his later years was a useless plea—having accepted the state's great charge, one serves until death.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to old age he never spoke of retirement for a single day. He once said Zeng Guofan's request to retire in his later years was a useless plea: having accepted the state's great charge, one serves until death.

sentences.zh: 馬關定約還，論者未已，或勸之歸。

translations.literal: When he returned from fixing the Shimonoseki treaty, critics had not ceased, and some urged him to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from fixing the Shimonoseki treaty, critics had not ceased, and some urged him to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 鴻章則言：「於國實有不能恝然之誼，今事敗求退，更誰賴乎？」

translations.literal: Hongzhang said: "Toward the state I truly cannot be indifferent; now that affairs have failed, if I seek to retire, on whom else can it rely?"
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang said, "Toward the state I truly cannot be indifferent. Now that affairs have failed, if I seek to retire, on whom else can it rely?"

sentences.zh: 其忠勤皆類此。

translations.literal: His loyalty and diligence were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His loyalty and diligence were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 居恆好整以暇，案上置宋搨蘭亭，日臨摹百字，飲食起居皆有恆晷。

translations.literal: In daily life he liked order and leisure; on his desk he placed a Song rubbing of the Lanting Preface and copied one hundred characters each day; eating, drinking, rising, and resting all kept fixed hours.
translations.idiomatic: In daily life he liked order and leisure. On his desk he placed a Song rubbing of the Lanting Preface and copied one hundred characters each day; eating, drinking, rising, and resting all kept fixed hours.

sentences.zh: 長於奏牘，時以曾、李並稱雲。

translations.literal: He excelled at memorials and dispatches; at the time Zeng and Li were spoken of together.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at memorials and dispatches; at the time Zeng and Li were spoken of together.

sentences.zh: 鴻章初以兄子經方為子，後生子經述，賞四品京堂，襲侯爵；

translations.literal: At first Hongzhang took his elder brother's son Jingfang as his son; later he bore Jingshu, who was awarded fourth-rank Beijing official and inherited the marquisate;
translations.idiomatic: At first Hongzhang took his elder brother's son Jingfang as his son. Later he bore Jingshu, who was awarded fourth-rank Beijing official and inherited the marquisate;

sentences.zh: 經邁，侍郎。

translations.literal: Jingmai became a vice-president.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmai became a vice-president.

sentences.zh: 論曰：中興名臣，與兵事相終始，其勳業往往為武功所掩。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Great ministers of the Restoration whose careers began and ended with military affairs often have their achievements overshadowed by martial glory.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Great ministers of the Restoration whose careers began and ended with military affairs often have their achievements overshadowed by martial glory.

sentences.zh: 鴻章既平大難，獨主國事數十年，內政外交，常以一身當其衝，國家倚為重輕，名滿全球，中外震仰，近世所未有也。

translations.literal: After Hongzhang had pacified the great calamity, he alone directed state affairs for decades; in domestic government and foreign relations he often bore the brunt alone. The state relied on him for weight; his name filled the globe; China and foreign lands looked up in awe—a thing without parallel in recent times.
translations.idiomatic: After Hongzhang had pacified the great calamity, he alone directed state affairs for decades. In domestic government and foreign relations he often bore the brunt alone. The state relied on him for weight; his name filled the globe; China and foreign lands looked up in awe—a thing without parallel in recent times.

sentences.zh: 生平以天下為己任，忍辱負重，庶不愧社稷之臣；

translations.literal: Throughout his life he took the realm as his own charge, bearing humiliation and heavy burdens—he may fairly be called a minister worthy of the altars of state;
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his life he took the realm as his own charge, bearing humiliation and heavy burdens. He may fairly be called a minister worthy of the altars of state;

sentences.zh: 惟才氣自喜，好以利祿驅眾，志節之士多不樂為用，緩急莫恃，卒致敗誤。

translations.literal: yet he delighted in his own talent, liked to drive the multitude with salary and rank, and men of firm principle were mostly unwilling to serve him; in crisis there was no one to rely on, and in the end defeat and error followed.
translations.idiomatic: yet he delighted in his own talent and liked to drive the multitude with salary and rank. Men of firm principle were mostly unwilling to serve him; in crisis there was no one to rely on, and defeat and error followed in the end.

sentences.zh: 疑謗之起，抑豈無因哉？

translations.literal: That suspicion and slander arose—was there not cause for it?
translations.idiomatic: That suspicion and slander arose—was there not cause for it?
